raw_response:
My family has been farming this land in Quzhou for three generations. I have about 15 mu — flat, loamy ground on the North China Plain. My father grew wheat and corn, I grow wheat and corn, and that's what I know how to do well.

Every year I do the same rotation: winter wheat goes in October after I rotary-till the maize stubble, and come June after wheat harvest I plant summer maize directly into the stubble without tilling — saves me time and keeps the soil from drying out too fast in the summer heat.

For wheat I use Jimai 22 — the agricultural station has promoted it for years and my neighbor gets good yields with it. I put down fertilizer at planting and top-dress at jointing. I irrigate four times: before winter sets in, at green-up, at jointing, and at heading. Water is getting harder to pump — my well is deeper every few years — but I can't risk a bad wheat crop. I spray herbicide in early spring and hit the aphids in May.

For maize I use a hybrid, Zhengdan 958, been using it for fifteen years. The summer rains help but I still irrigate at seedling stage and again at silking if it's dry. One or two pesticide passes for corn borer or armyworm.

I won't change what's working. At 54 I'm not going to experiment with vegetables or cotton — too much labor, too much price risk. Grain is stable. Government buys it.
